newsitem.title: USA: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.
newsitem.headline: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets looked at 1630 GMT on Friday.
UNITED STATES - The U.S. Treasuries market was closed for the Independence Day holiday. The market will resume trading on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures ended the week little changed, using Friday's quiet session as a period of consolidation. But analysts said the outlook for the market was positive, with the Bund future set to head towards historical highs in the medium term.
Futures: September Bunds on LIFFE at 102.4, down 0.02
September Euromarks at 96.84, unchanged.
Cash: 10-year Bund yield 5.6 percent.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended higher in low volume trade, with the long end of the curve making solid gains despite a dull day on the markets, traders said. "The long end did extremely well, they put in a very good performance while the rest drifted off with lack of interest," one trader said.
Futures: September Long gilts on LIFFE at 114.78, up 0.31
September Eurosterling at 92.84, up 0.01
Cash: 10-year gilt yield 7.01 percent.
FRANCE - 10-yr bond futures settle in positive territory but shave gains toward session close on profit-taking after market boosted early in day by big purchases.
Futures: September Long bond on MATIF at 129.98, up 0.02
September PIBOR at 96.57, unchanged
Cash: 10-year bond (OAT) yield 5.48 percent.

ITALY - BTP futures pared back earlier gains as trading wound down ahead of the weekend but dealers said good support seen in the 135.50/40 area was a positive signal. The September Liffe contract ended three basis points up at 135.58 after earlier setting a new high at 135.84. The Bund spread had also narrowed to a new 101 bps low.
Futures: September Long bond on LIFFE at 135.65, up 0.1
September Eurolira at 93.5, down 0.01
Cash: 10-year bond (BTP) yield 6.61 percent.

JAPAN - Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rose to close at two-month highs as dealers started to believe it unlikely that Japan would raise interest rates in the near future. Such views spread especially after U.S. Treasuries rose overnight and prompted two major domestic banks to buy fixed interest rates in the Interest Rate Swap (IRS) market this morning, traders said.
Futures: September JGB future on LIFFE compared with Tokyo close at 125.13, up 0.39
September Euroyen at 99.33, unchanged
Cash: 10-year JGB yield 2.5 percent.

EUROBONDS - Issuance slowed due to the Independence Day holiday in the U.S. Bankers said few firm deals were lined up for next week, but the market's mood was positive. Five-year dollar bonds were expected, as well as 10-year mark paper after a successful 3.0 billion mark bond from Italy. NTT Corp is due to launch a 10-year Euroyen bond.
